overall: The checker passes (423/423), and most items are true, neutral and well pitched; the token classes are sound (12 exclusive team/league/position tokens are right; spot-checked bunt and inning). The main problem is no-space capitalized tokens (Cricket, Pit, Players, Saber, Surface, part of Slide) forced in with quotes or capitals that read unnaturally: drop them and accept fewer items with a note rather than force them. Softball sport facts (underhand pitching, Olympic history) give a baseball fan an advantage; only the softball-question idiom is safe. The same goes for cricket catch-out items. A recurring smaller issue is a token sitting in a throwaway clause (Electricians..., X vary; ..., Hamlet must decide...; ice cap/Greenland; pitting/rust), where the question works without it. Fix these by making the token-bearing phrase the point. There are a few giveaways where the answer echoes the question (Advantage/disadvantage, corner arc, Caught/catches, Brick/brickbats, #/hashtagged), several same-template sets (proceeded, reshaped, built-and-maintained, segregation for blacks), and three joke-distractor items.
